Teacher side

3 changes
Sections

A section now carries its school year

What the panel asked

“Sa create section sir sa DASHBOARD pwede na — Create Section, School Year * [ 2026–2027 ], Section Name * [ Grade 3 - Gals ].”

“Tapos if naa ka sa section sidebar i click sir kay: Grade 3 - Gals / 36 Students / SY 2026–2027 / Created July 21, 2026.”

What shipped

  • Create Section takes School Year then Section Name, defaulting to the current SY (June–March).
  • Rejected unless the years are consecutive — 2026-2027, not 2026-2030.
  • Section cards read name, student count, SY 2026–2027, and the created date in full.
  • New column classrooms.school_year; the unique key moved to (teacher, name, school_year) so a section name can be reused next year.
  • Existing sections were backfilled from their creation date.
Enrollment

Registrar class list: review first, then confirm

What the panel asked

“Sa Student Enrollment, naa tay ‘Upload Official Class List (CSV)’ button, with the note ‘Upload the official student list provided by the Registrar.’ … i-display sa MindSpark ang mga student records nga naa sa file for review. Below the displayed student list, naa tay ‘Cancel’ ug ‘Confirm Enrollment’ buttons.”

“Ang SYSTEM ang automatically mo-generate sa unique username ug default password sa matag student (Username: generated username, Password: username + 123) … together with an ‘Export Login Credentials (CSV)’ button.”

What shipped

  • Picking a file enrolls nothing — it renders the records in a review table with the file name and count.
  • Cancel discards the file so another can be picked; Confirm Enrollment commits.
  • Usernames are generated by MindSpark: first initial + last name, stripped to letters and digits, with a numeric suffix on collision (jsantos, jsantos2). Password is username + "123".
  • Collisions are checked against every account in the system, not just the file.
  • The class list only needs Last / First / Middle Name — no username or password column.
  • Success message lists each generated credential, with Export Login Credentials (CSV) to hand out and keep.
  1. Create section
  2. Open section
  3. Upload class list
  4. Review records
  5. Confirm enrollment
  6. Accounts generated
  7. Export credentials
Enrollment

Manual enrollment splits the name into three fields

What the panel asked

“Sa manual enrollment, himuon siya ug Last Name, First Name, Middle Name, Username, ug Password instead of Full Name lang.”

“Dile siya hawaon sa system sir kay need japun siya” — manual enrollment stays; only the name fields change.

What shipped

  • Manual enrollment kept, now with Last Name, First Name, Middle Name, Username, Password and a section picker.
  • The same three fields replaced “Full Name” in the student account editor.
  • full_name is still written, composed as “First Middle Last”, so reports, the roster and the game profile read unchanged.
  • Last and First are required; each part is capped at 60 characters.

Student game side

2 changes
Level Complete

Three popups collapsed into one Level Complete screen

What the panel asked

“Daghan kaayu ug i click sir bago mag proceed sa next level … After sa Level Up animation, isa nalang ka screen for the Result, Trophy, and Badges.”

“If wala siyay badge nga na-earn sa level, i-hide nalang completely ang badge section para dili naay blank space … If 1–2 badges, side-by-side lang; if 3–4 badges, compact layout like 2x2.”

Flow: Level Up → Level Complete / Result + Trophy + Badges → Retry / Map / Next.

What shipped

  • The trophy → summary → badges sequence is gone. The Level Up animation plays over the dying boss for 3 seconds, then one screen opens.
  • Result, Trophy and Badges sit side by side: correct answers, stars, points, hearts on the left; trophy centre; newly earned badges right.
  • With no new badges the badge panel is removed from the DOM — the remaining two columns widen to fill the row. No reserved blank space.
  • One badge stands alone, two sit side by side, three or four compact into a 2×2.
  • Retry, Map and Next are on that same screen — one click to the next level.
  • The Level Up animation gained shockwave rings, rotating light rays and a 16-particle burst.
  • Sized to fit a landscape phone without scrolling; the global .game-screen img rule that was forcing artwork to full size is now overridden for result art.
Badges

A badge appears once, on the level that earned it

What the panel asked

“Once ma-earn na sa student ang usa ka badge, dili na siya mo-appear balik sa next levels … Kana ra nga newly earned badges ang ipakita sa Level Summary.”

“Once ma-earn ang badge, i-save siya sa profile/database.”

What shipped

  • The result screen reads a per-run list of badges first earned during that level, not the student's whole collection.
  • The list is cleared when a level is entered, retried, or advanced to — a retry can only re-show what that attempt actually earned.
  • Awards are written to student_badges with INSERT IGNORE, so a second award is a no-op and never re-announced.
  • Mid-level awards (Math Streak, granted per answer) still toast during play and then appear in that level's summary.
  • The full collection stays visible on the profile and in the map banner — Trophies: 1/5 · Badges: 4/7.
  • Forest Champion remains the capstone, unlocked only once the other six are held.
